articles.title: SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7
articles.snippet:
SWEN Capital Partners closed SWEN PE Select Europa 7 at €236 million. The fund is the seventh vintage of SWEN's European multi-strategy private equity program, which has invested directly and indirectly alongside European private equity managers since 2008.
The post SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7 appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7
SWEN Capital Partners closed SWEN PE Select Europa 7 at €236 million. The fund is the seventh vintage of SWEN’s European multi-strategy private equity program, which has invested directly and indirectly alongside European private equity managers since 2008.
At final close, approximately 80% of the fund had already been committed to underlying investments.
SWEN expects to continue making commitments through the end of 2026 and into the first half of 2027.
Through an overcommitment mechanism, the fund can make commitments equal to as much as 120% of its capital base.
That gives Europa 7 capacity for approximately €283 million of total investment commitments.
The strategy combines primary fund commitments, secondary transactions, and minority direct investments.
Its target allocation is approximately 50% to primary investments, 20% to secondaries, and 30% to minority direct investments.
The structure is designed to provide diversified access to specialist European private equity managers and portfolio companies while allowing SWEN to manage pacing, manager selection, and diversification.
Europa 7 is similar in size to its three immediate predecessors.
Europa 4 raised €261 million, Europa 5 raised €240 million, and Europa 6 raised €255 million.
Europa 7 is also the first fund in the series classified as Article 9 under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation.
SWEN said the vehicle is one of the relatively few European Article 9 private equity fund-of-funds strategies focused on small and mid-sized companies.

articles.title: Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering
articles.snippet:
Arda Industries has emerged from stealth with $232 million in total funding to develop AI software that helps manufacturers turn new product designs into working assembly lines and update those lines as designs change. The company is targeting a long-term vision of robotic assembly lines that can adapt at software speed.
The post Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering
Arda Industries has emerged from stealth with $232 million in total funding to develop AI software that helps manufacturers turn new product designs into working assembly lines and update those lines as designs change. The company is targeting a long-term vision of robotic assembly lines that can adapt at software speed.
Arda’s financing includes a $160 million Series A at a $1.5 billion valuation, co-led by Altimeter, Accel, and Khosla Ventures, with participation from XYZ Venture Capital, 8VC, SV Angel, and Felicis. The round follows a $72 million seed led by Accel and Founders Fund, with Khosla Ventures and XYZ Venture Capital also participating.
The company’s AI agent reads CAD files and other design artifacts and generates manufacturing-engineering work that would otherwise require teams to determine assembly order, write work instructions, and lay out production stations. Arda said the software is already deployed at Anduril Industries through its ArsenalOS manufacturing software.
According to Arda, basic work instructions that previously took 10 hours can be produced in about 15 minutes, while more complex engineering workflows that could take up to 30 hours have been reduced to roughly 2.5 hours. The company is initially focused on defense and the data-center supply chain, including manufacturers of transformers and electrical equipment.
Arda is also prototyping AI agents that can program robots to execute its assembly plans. The goal is to reduce the months of custom engineering often required to reprogram automation when products change. Arda will use the funding to expand engineering and research, grow deployments across manufacturing sectors, and develop robotics models for automated assembly.
KEY QUOTES:
“I kept asking: why can we design the next generation of products in America, but not build them here? When a product changes every year, the factory has to be able to change with it. Manufacturing leaders told me their products change constantly, and manufacturing engineering can’t keep pace. Their designs change at software speed, but their factories don’t. So, we built the technology platform that solves this problem. Today, U.S. manufacturers designing innovative consumer hardware products at scale can only make them in Asia. Imagine a fully automated version of Shenzhen in West Texas – that’s what we want to make possible.”
Bob McGrew, Founder And CEO Of Arda
“Our manufacturing engineers are doing two hard things at once. They’re keeping up with design teams that iterate constantly, and they’re scaling production to meet demand. Arda helps them get design changes onto the floor faster and catch potential issues sooner. We would be behind on our production goals without it.”
Matt Grimm, Co-Founder And COO Of Anduril Industries

articles.title: Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs
articles.snippet:
Lockheed Martin has received four U.S. Department of Defense contract awards and modifications with a combined value of more than $226 million, supporting Apache attack helicopters, naval electronic warfare systems, and multiple F-35 programs.
The post Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs
Lockheed Martin has received four U.S. Department of Defense contract awards and modifications with a combined value of more than $226 million, supporting Apache attack helicopters, naval electronic warfare systems, and multiple F-35 programs.
The largest award is a $117,118,040 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for Generation II radar frequency interferometer post-production support services for Apache attack helicopters. The contract includes cost-no-fee, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and firm-fixed-price components.
Work locations and funding for the Apache-related contract will be determined as individual orders are issued, with the overall effort expected to continue through October 12, 2031. One bid was solicited and one was received. Army Contracting Command at Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity under contract W58RGZ-27-D-A007.
Lockheed Martin’s Rotary and Mission Systems business also received a $74,294,440 firm-fixed-price modification for production of Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program AN/SLQ-32(V)6 systems. The award includes Foreign Military Sales purchases for Canada, representing 52% of the work, and Japan, representing 47%, along with a 1% purchase for the U.S. Coast Guard.
Approximately $38.4 million in fiscal 2026 Canadian FMS funding, $35.4 million in Japanese FMS funding, and $457,768 in fiscal 2025 Coast Guard procurement funding will be obligated. Work will be performed primarily in Liverpool, New York, and Lansdale, Pennsylvania, through September 2029.
Separately, Lockheed Martin received a $16,111,551 modification supporting avionics test capabilities, cybersecurity modernization, and specialized repair infrastructure for the F-35 Integrated Core Processor. The work also covers engineering, program management, planning, readiness reviews, and introduction-to-service activities intended to support fleet operational readiness.
That F-35 effort will be split evenly between McKinney, Texas, and Palm Bay, Florida, and is expected to be completed in January 2029. Approximately $8.1 million each in fiscal 2026 Air Force and Navy aircraft procurement funding will be obligated.
Lockheed Martin Aeronautics also received an $18,789,801 contract modification for system development, demonstration, and integration supporting an F-35 aircraft variant tailored for an unspecified Foreign Military Sales customer.
Approximately 80% of that work will take place in Fort Worth, Texas, with the remaining 20% at undisclosed locations in the continental U.S. Completion is expected in December 2030, with the full $18.8 million being funded by the FMS customer.
Together, the awards expand Lockheed Martin’s work across rotary-wing survivability and sensing, maritime electronic warfare, F-35 cybersecurity and sustainment infrastructure, and international F-35 development.

articles.snippet:
Neogen reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $222.8 million, representing growth of 6.5% and core growth of 8.1%.
The post Neogen: Q1 Revenue Rises 6.5% To $222.8 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Neogen: Q1 Revenue Rises 6.5% To $222.8 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Neogen: Q1 Revenue Rises 6.5% To $222.8 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance
Neogen reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $222.8 million, representing growth of 6.5% and core growth of 8.1%.
Food Safety revenue increased 7.4%, including core growth of 8.1%.
Animal Safety revenue increased 4.2%, with core growth of 8%.
Gross margin increased to 47.4% from 45.4%.
Adjusted gross margin was 49.8% compared with 49.5% a year earlier.
Neogen reported a net loss of $11.9 million, or $0.05 per share.
Adjusted net income increased to $17.5 million, or $0.08 per diluted share, from $9.5 million, or $0.04 per share, a year earlier.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $41.6 million from $35.5 million.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 18.7% from 17%.
Operating cash flow totaled $12.9 million, and free cash flow reached $4.7 million.
Neogen remains on schedule to begin producing saleable Petrifilm products at its Lansing manufacturing site in November 2026.
The company completed validation of its first Petrifilm SKU in August.
Neogen also announced a collaboration and equity investment in Hinalea Imaging to develop hyperspectral digital imaging solutions for food safety and quality inspection.
The company continues working toward the sale of its global Genomics business to Zoetis, with regulatory reviews expected to conclude by the end of December.
Neogen raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to between $885 million and $890 million from $880 million to $885 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $181 million to $183 million from $180 million to $182 million.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our first-quarter results reflect encouraging progress as the changes underway across the organization continue to take hold.”
“We are strengthening commercial discipline, harmonizing our sales operating model, rebuilding our innovation engine and improving the systems and processes that support inventory optimization and customer service.”
Mike Nassif, President and CEO of Neogen
